elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim..." — express defence duty extending to affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: "indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "Vendor's breach of Applicable Law", using the Section 1.2 defined term.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (d): "Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct"; both categories captured.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "Customer shall give Vendor written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "Vendor shall control its defence and settlement" — control expressly allocated to Vendor as indemnitor.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: "Any indemnity given by Customer under this Agreement is limited to third-party claims arising from content Customer provides to Vendor and Customer's breach of Applicable Law." No pre-existing Customer indemnity exists to contradict this cap.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same inserted limb (a) covering third-party IP infringement/misappropriation allegations against the Services or Deliverables.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; the insertion contains no modification exclusion, which is more favourable to Customer and does not breach a permission.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion is imposed, so the condition allowing (but not requiring) it does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification-based exclusion appears, which is acceptable and Customer-favourable.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: The inserted clause contains no procure/modify/replace remedy obligation; no other provision supplies one (Section 9.3 refers to "remedies required by Section 20.5", which does not exist).

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop appears anywhere in the inserted or retained language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No cap is stated; Section 21.3 treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims (uncapped), so no 3x super-cap exists.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: all ten preferred elements are met in operative language (defence and indemnity for Customer and its Affiliates; IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs; notice, Vendor control, reasonable cooperation; and an express cap on any Customer indemnity).

Fallback is incomplete (procure/modify/replace, refund backstop and 3x super-cap all absent), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully met; targeting preferred is also correct since Section 21.3 already makes indemnification obligations Excluded Claims, so importing a 3x cap would cut back existing protection.

Minimality holds: the finding is a missing-clause insertion, all added words map to selected preferred elements (indemnity limbs, procedure, Customer-indemnity limitation), and no survival tail, at-own-expense wording, extra damages categories, or unrelated deletions were introduced. Retained Sections 9.3, 19.5 and 21.3 are untouched.

Drafting repairs to tidy (not element failures): (i) the insertion is rendered without a section number — number it as Section 20 (and its subsections) so the retained cross-reference in Section 9.3 to "the remedies required by Section 20.5" resolves; consider adding a 20.5 procure/modify/replace/refund remedy so that Customer's Section 9.3 termination trigger is operable; (ii) confirm "Affiliates" and "Deliverables"/"Customer Data" are defined terms in Section 1 — if "Affiliate" is not defined, use lowercase "affiliates" to avoid a dangling defined term.
